content: 1. Oxcarbazepine reduces the levels or effects of elvitegravir by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with CYP3A inducers may decrease plasma concentrations of elvitegravir and/or a concomitantly administered protease inhibitor, potentially leading to therapeutic failure and resistance. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of oxycodone by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification or close monitoring is necessary. If co-administering CYP3A4 inhibitors with fentanyl, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals and consider fentanyl dose adjustments until stable drug effects are achieved. 3. Cobicistat increases the toxicity of ozanimod by mechanisms involving other pathways. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of ozanimod (a BCRP substrate) with BCRP inhibitors increases the exposure of both minor and major active metabolites of ozanimod, which may heighten the risk of adverse reactions. Close monitoring is required. 4. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Similarly, cobicistat increases the levels or effects of protein-bound paclitaxel through the same mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 5. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for significant adverse effects. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 7. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. 8. Cobicistat increases the levels of panobinostat by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification or close monitoring is necessary. Reduce the starting dose of panobinostat to 10 mg if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Close monitoring is essential. 9. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of paricalcitol by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of paroxetine through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor its response during co-administration with SSRIs and cobicistat. 11. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pemigatinib dose may be resumed. 13. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with CYP3A inducers may decrease plasma concentrations of elvitegravir and/or a concomitantly administered protease inhibitor, leading to therapeutic failure and resistance. 14. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with CYP3A inducers may decrease plasma concentrations of elvitegravir and/or a concomitantly administered protease inhibitor, leading to therapeutic failure and resistance. 15. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for lack or loss of virologic response from cobicistat. 16. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with CYP3A inducers may decrease plasma concentrations of elvitegravir and/or a concomitantly administered protease inhibitor, leading to therapeutic failure and resistance. 17. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for lack or loss of virologic response from cobicistat. 18. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pimavanserin by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Decrease the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 19. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pimozide by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for increased systemic exposure to pimozide, which raises the risk of QT prolongation. 20. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pirtobrutinib by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib for the duration of strong CYP3A inhibitor use. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for five half-lives, resume the previous pirtobrutinib dose. 21. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pitavastatin by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification or close monitoring is necessary. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with cobicistat, start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate. Co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor may increase unconjugated MMAE AUC, potentially heightening polatuzumab vedotin toxicities. 23. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ponatinib by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 24. Posaconazole increases the levels of elvitegravir by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 26. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pralsetinib by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 27. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pravastatin by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification or close monitoring is necessary. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with cobicistat, start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. 28. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of praziquantel by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with CYP3A inducers may decrease plasma concentrations of elvitegravir and/or a concomitantly administered protease inhibitor, leading to therapeutic failure and resistance. 30. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This combination is contraindicated. 31. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of progesterone intravaginal gel by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 32. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of progesterone micronized by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 33. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 34. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of propafenone by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Clinical monitoring is recommended upon co-administration with antiarrhythmics. 35. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of protriptyline through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor its response during co-administration with TCAs and cobicistat. 36. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of quazepam by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Cobicistat increases the levels of quetiapine by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, reduce the quetiapine dose to one-sixth of the current dose and monitor for quetiapine-associated adverse reactions. Refer to quetiapine prescribing information for initial dosing and titration. 38. Quinidine increases the levels of elvitegravir by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of quinidine through other mechanisms. Therapy modification or close monitoring is necessary. Quinidine is a substrate of CYP3A4 and P-gp and inhibits CYP2D6 and P-gp. Cobicistat is a substrate and inhibitor of both isoenzymes and a P-gp inhibitor. 40. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of quinine by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of quizartinib by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification or close monitoring is necessary. Reduce the quizartinib dose to 20 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If the current dose is 20 mg daily, interrupt quizartinib for the duration of strong CYP3A inhibitor use. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for five half-lives, resume the previous quizartinib dose. 42. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of rabeprazole by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This combination is contraindicated. 44. Regorafenib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF through other mechanisms. Therapy modification or close monitoring is necessary. Regorafenib likely inhibits BCRP (ABCG2) transport. Co-administration with a BCRP substrate may increase systemic exposure to the substrate and related toxicity. 45. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of repaglinide by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3-5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 47. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of resmetirom through other mechanisms. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of resmetirom (an OATP1B1/3 substrate) with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. 48. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by altering the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 49. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ribociclib by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug.
